incidents.victim: ATB Market, Tez Tour, Dodo Pizza
incidents.vector: Attackers found valid credentials in Dodo Pizza's GitHub repositories and used them to access backend systems across multiple companies, stealing data and destroying systems before demanding ransoms.
incidents.impact: Three organizations across Ukraine and Russia breached; data exfiltrated and systems destroyed. Three of four gang members arrested in Russia and Belarus; one 19-year-old suspect placed under house arrest facing up to six years.

incidents.victim: BAE Systems / US Federal Bankruptcy Courts
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on BAE Systems compromised the Bankruptcy Noticing Center, the platform BAE operates on behalf of all US federal bankruptcy courts.
incidents.impact: All federal bankruptcy court notice production halted nationwide; BNC websites offline including bnc.uscourts.gov. Scope of any data theft under investigation. Incident follows separate attacks on DOT contractor and the FBI.

incidents.victim: UK Legal Aid Agency
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in the Legal Aid Agency's IT systems to gain unauthorized access and exfiltrate unstructured data from its online service, initially breached prior to May 2025.
incidents.impact: October 15 update revealed 250,000 records pre-dating 2007 (earliest from 1978) included, raising total affected individuals above 2 million. Stolen data includes criminal histories, financial assessments, bank account details, and probation records. UK government has refused ransom; hackers claim 2M+ records.

incidents.victim: Ledger cryptocurrency wallet users
incidents.vector: Hardware supply chain attack: LTE modules with SIM cards were professionally soldered into Ledger Nano X wallets by a compromised Southeast Asian reseller (CryptoBilis), intercepting seed phrases and transmitting them to attackers.
incidents.impact: Up to $100 million in cryptocurrency stolen from affected wallet holders since spring 2026. Implants confirmed in devices sold through Asian resellers and MediaMarkt stores in Europe. Ledger directed all customers to move funds off affected devices.

incidents.victim: Al Jazeera employees (and potentially EU governments, NATO, UN networks)
incidents.vector: Israeli advertising company Discover-Tech deployed Candiru commercial spyware payloads via targeted online advertisements; CitizenLab confirmed device infections at Al Jazeera headquarters.
incidents.impact: Confirmed device compromises at Al Jazeera HQ. Ad cluster analysis indicates likely targeting of EU governments, NATO, UN networks, global news organizations, and semiconductor manufacturers. Google removed Discover-Tech from ad platforms; IAB Europe suspended its membership.

incidents.victim: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's inner circle
incidents.vector: Unknown attacker gained access to phones belonging to members of PM Netanyahu's inner circle and exfiltrated personal photos and videos.
incidents.impact: Photos and videos from the PM's spouse, Israel's Ambassador to the UAE, and a senior PM adviser were leaked publicly two weeks before Israeli elections on October 27. Haaretz independently verified some leaked content.

incidents.victim: FLC consortium (Fehmarn Belt fixed link project)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeted FLC, the international consortium building the Fehmarn Belt fixed link — the world's longest road and rail tunnel under construction between Denmark and Germany.
incidents.impact: Tunnel construction halted; some equipment systems and employee access cards affected. Project timeline impact unknown.

incidents.victim: 75,000+ organizations in 150 countries (healthcare, financial services, IT)
incidents.vector: Chinese-language phishing-as-a-service infrastructure (YAM Store / CoGUI / Iron Man System) provided customizable phishing kits to criminal operators targeting organizations worldwide since January 2026.
incidents.impact: Over 1 billion malicious messages sent to 75,000+ organizations across 150 countries. Microsoft and Health-ISAC filed civil lawsuit against operator Yang Jian (d/b/a Yam Store); Microsoft seized and redirected infrastructure, disabled 20,000+ accounts, and blocked 100,000+ domains.

incidents.victim: Intermarché and other French supermarket chains
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited Danfoss refrigeration and freezer equipment running outdated firmware with default credentials unchanged, remotely raising temperatures across hundreds of stores.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of Intermarché and other French supermarkets affected; tens of millions of euros in food stock losses. ACSC and cybersecurity researchers issued advisories on OT/refrigeration vulnerabilities.

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Albert Heijn, Delhaize, and others)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeted Ahold Delhaize's centralized online ordering and logistics platform over the weekend.
incidents.impact: Supermarket chains taken offline across the US (Food Lion, Stop & Shop), Netherlands (Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall), Belgium (Delhaize), and Romania (Profi, Mega Image). Millions of customers unable to place online orders.

incidents.victim: OpenAI
incidents.vector: A Saudi national OpenAI employee planted a covert LTE-enabled listening device behind a TV in a conference room at OpenAI's San Francisco headquarters; a second device was found unattended in a building.
incidents.impact: Extent of information captured undetermined. OpenAI states no evidence of unauthorized access to model weights, source code, or customer data. Employee arrested by FBI and terminated. FTC launched inquiry into AI company security incidents.

incidents.victim: 70+ US companies (healthcare, communications, cybersecurity, retail, manufacturing)
incidents.vector: North Korean nationals used laptop farms to masquerade as US remote workers, gaining employment at US companies to generate revenue for the North Korean state and potentially access sensitive systems.
incidents.impact: Over $3 million generated for North Korean government programs. 40 laptop farms in Texas disrupted; 187 laptops seized. DOJ indicted 14 individuals and arrested two. Sectors impacted include healthcare, communications, and cybersecurity.

incidents.victim: Global critical infrastructure (government, manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, education)
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked cyber operator (Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: Chinese government-linked company Integrity Technology Group operated a botnet enabling Chinese state cyber actors to conduct reconnaissance and intrusions targeting government and critical infrastructure globally.
incidents.impact: Ongoing intrusion campaign affecting government services, critical manufacturing, healthcare, IT, and education across Southeast Asia, Africa, and North America. NSA, FBI, UK NCSC, and partners from Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain issued joint advisory.

incidents.victim: MrMax Holdings (Japanese discount retailer)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized third-party access to MrMax app and online store servers via unspecified intrusion, discovered October 3, 2026.
incidents.impact: Up to 1,735,154 member records exposed including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and membership IDs. Company states no credit card data or passwords were compromised. Services temporarily suspended.

incidents.victim: FBI (Federal Bureau of Investigation)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 using a WAF bypass technique; Accenture, the platform manager, had failed to apply the security patch explicitly issued to secure the system.
incidents.impact: Sensitive personal data of thousands of FBI employees exposed, including job details, home addresses, medical records, and intelligence role assignments. Accenture contractor removed from FBI. Multiple ShinyHunters suspects subsequently arrested: leader detained in Jordan, one arrested in Netherlands, one in Pennsylvania.

incidents.victim: 395 organizations (440+ PaperCut instances)
incidents.vector: Russia-linked threat actors used AI-automated agents to conduct broad, automated exploitation of vulnerable PaperCut NG/MF print management software at scale.
incidents.impact: 440+ vulnerable PaperCut instances compromised across 395 organizations in an AI-assisted campaign. Scope of data theft or system access undisclosed.

incidents.victim: Meta (Facebook parent company)
incidents.vector: Threat actor used a Meta employee's stolen credentials to gain unauthorized access to Meta's GitHub repositories and exfiltrate employee data and portions of source code.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 1,500+ US employees stolen. Some Meta source code exfiltrated. Company began notifying affected employees.

incidents.victim: Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing aviation subsidiary)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters breached Jeppesen ForeFlight, a Boeing spin-off providing aviation navigation software, and demanded extortion payment.
incidents.impact: Data exfiltrated and extortion demands made. Breach extent not publicly disclosed. Part of a broader ShinyHunters campaign targeting multiple high-profile organizations.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations (legal, SaaS, BPO, technology, government)
incidents.vector: Exploited a zero-day authentication bypass in BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances (CVE-2026-102764) to gain root access, deploy custom SAWFLY webshell and BARECLAW tunneler, and harvest all stored credentials.
incidents.impact: Credential vault contents exfiltrated; persistent implants installed surviving configuration resets. Group known to follow selective zero-day use with broad exploitation post-disclosure. BeyondTrust patch released Oct 8; widespread exploitation expected for unpatched systems.

incidents.victim: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
incidents.vector: Rhysida ransomware gang gained unauthorized access to a subset of Anne Arundel County government systems and exfiltrated files.
incidents.impact: 2.6 TB of files allegedly stolen; $2 million ransom demanded. Investigation ongoing to determine if resident data is included. County hosts offices of DOD, IRS, EPA, Social Security Administration, and US Coast Guard.

incidents.victim: Government organizations across CIS (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, others)
incidents.vector: Macro-enabled documents delivered PS2EXE PowerShell downloaders with second-stage payloads hosted on GitHub; also exploited WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 to gain initial access to target systems.
incidents.impact: Multi-year espionage campaign against CIS government entities focused on diplomatic and water/energy sector data. Cisco Talos attributes with medium confidence to a Kazakhstan-nexus threat actor (UAT-6275).

incidents.victim: US Embassy in Fiji
incidents.vector: Chinese hackers breached the US Embassy in Fiji's network and maintained persistent access for approximately two months.
incidents.impact: Embassy network compromised July through August 2026. US government notified Fiji government and provided technical indicators for Fiji's own investigation of possible parallel intrusions.

incidents.victim: Government entities (multiple countries)
incidents.vector: AI-generated custom malware payloads, SysGoRAT remote access trojan, web shells, and credential harvesting tools used to compromise Linux-based government infrastructure over six months.
incidents.impact: Mailbox contents and database records exfiltrated from government networks. Attribution unclear between nation-state and sophisticated criminal actors. Campaign discovered and reported by Palo Alto Unit 42.

incidents.victim: Telecom managed service provider and 500+ client organizations
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2024-47575 (FortiJump) against a centralized FortiManager to exfiltrate firewall configurations for 500+ managed FortiGate clients; later returned to deploy novel PEERSTITCH memory-resident ARM64 implant via CVE-2025-61624.
incidents.impact: Network configurations of 500+ managed customer organizations exfiltrated. Novel PEERSTITCH implant survived device reboots, providing persistent access. Downstream exposure risks for all MSP customers. CISA added CVE-2025-61624 to KEV catalog Oct 16.
